about: Generic FDM and fastener rules for --mode assembly. No number here is specific to any request or enclosure: request numbers come from the request/L1 text and part numbers from benchmarks/enclosure/parts/*/part.json. Every value carries its source. Values used in a design are recorded with provenance 'rules:<key>'. This file is reviewed by hand (test_no_hardcoding does not scan JSON).

sliding_fit_min.source: FDM practice: minimum per-side clearance for a sliding fit with a 0.4 mm nozzle (requirements.md A11)

sliding_fit_max.source: FDM practice: maximum per-side clearance before a fit rattles (requirements.md A11)

board_to_wall.source: default clearance between a board edge and a printed wall when the request is silent (requirements.md A11)

plug_to_opening.source: clearance between a cable plug envelope and its wall opening (FDM hole shrinkage plus plug tolerance)

opening_oversize_max.source: default maximum opening oversize beyond the plug envelope when the request is silent

min_ligament.source: minimum printed material between an opening and an edge or another opening (about 4 perimeters at 0.4 mm)

overhang_angle_deg.source: FDM practice: steepest unsupported overhang measured from vertical

bridge_max.source: FDM practice: longest reliable bridge in PLA/PETG

round_hole_exempt_max.source: FDM practice: round holes in vertical walls up to this diameter print without support

fn.source: $fn for round features, same as cad_agent.SEGMENTS

standoff_wall_min.source: printed material around a pilot hole (4 perimeters)

component_height_default.source: keep-out above a populated board when the request gives no height: tallest common through-hole parts (electrolytics, trimmers) - used only when the request is silent, flagged as an assumption

solder_side_default.source: solder fillets plus clipped leads below a through-hole board - used only when the request is silent, flagged as an assumption

keepout_margin.source: margin added to an estimated keep-out height

plug_travel.source: length a cable plug envelope is swept outward past its overmold so it runs 'past any wall' (several wall thicknesses plus a hand gripping the plug)

driver_clearance.source: radial room around a pan screw head for the driver bit and its wobble (seat column = head diameter + 2 x this)

driver_diameter.source: shaft of a common #1 Phillips / 2.5 mm hex screwdriver plus wobble

driver_reach.source: screwdriver shaft length above the base rim with the lid off: V-DRIVER runs from the board top to the rim plus this (requirements.md V-DRIVER); a generic tool length

design_margin.source: setpoint offset inside one-sided clearance limits: 5 x the judge's 0.02 mm measurement epsilon (rubric.md 3.2), so tessellation and rounding never flip a pass; derivation targets only, checks keep their limits (ARCHITECTURE.md 7.7)

grid_search_step.source: coarse step of the grid-feasibility search over one pitch cell (ARCHITECTURE.md 7.9): a measurement resolution 1/15 of grid_residual_max and the judge's 0.01 mm reporting precision; each result is refined locally below 1e-9 mm

grid_residual_max.source: a 0.64 mm square pin in a ~1.0 mm plated hole: lateral slack before the pin no longer drops into the grid hole (requirements.md A7)

overlap_max.source: largest overlap of two printed bodies in the closed pose that is still numerical contact, not interpenetration (requirements.md L3.7.1.2; cad_checks.OVERLAP_VOLUME)

interference_max.source: largest intersection of two reference parts counted as touching (requirements.md R7)

seat_gap_max.source: largest gap between a board's underside and a standoff top for the board to count as seated (requirements.md seating rule)

seat_axis_residual_max.source: largest board-hole to pilot-axis offset for a screw to start straight (requirements.md seating rule)

lip_engagement.source: FDM practice: height a locating lid lip overlaps the base wall (about 10 layers)

lip_wall.source: three 0.4 mm perimeters: the thinnest lip that prints stiff

boss_wall_min.source: printed material around a lid-screw pilot (4 perimeters), same as standoff_wall_min

cut_overrun.source: a cut runs this far past each face it must clear, so no zero-thickness skin is left

screw_hole_clearance_min.source: ISO 273 medium series: radial clearance of a screw through a hole (M2.5 -> 2.9, M3 -> 3.4)

given_hole_clearance_min.source: radial clearance a screw needs through a board's existing mounting hole: the hole is a fixed datum, so a screw passes it when its major diameter fits (requirements.md A9: 'M2 passes the 2.0 holes'); ISO 273 clearance (screw_hole_clearance_min) applies only to holes the design makes

max_quantity.source: largest quantity of one catalogue part offered to the controller per request

part_to_wall.source: smallest gap between a placed module (with its headers) and a printed surface: FDM dimensional tolerance plus assembly slop

measure_tol.source: measurement tolerance of the agent's own checks: half the judge's 0.02 mm (rubric.md 3.2), so the agent is the stricter of the two

margin_scale.source: normalisation length of check margins (margin 1.0 = 1 mm of slack)

lookup_k.source: catalogue candidates offered per part kind

view_elevation_deg.source: camera elevation above horizontal for the elevation renders of assembly mode, so openings show

arrange_rank_max.source: generic cap on controller-ranked layout candidates (feasible edge assignments ConfirmArrangement scores); reported in design.json when it truncates

layout_step.source: step of the 1-D shift search that resolves a placement collision

aperture_min_volume.source: aperture regions smaller than this are numerical slivers, not openings (rubric.md 3.4)

parity_volume_rel.source: OpenSCAD vs manifold3d volume agreement for the delivered mesh (ARCHITECTURE.md 3.2)

parity_bbox.source: OpenSCAD vs manifold3d bounding-box agreement for the delivered mesh (ARCHITECTURE.md 3.2)

spec_slots.about: Generic enclosure spec slots. The controller maps each slot onto one number occurrence that Python extracted from the request or L1 text (or 'none'); a 'none' slot takes its default_rule value and is flagged as an assumption. A slot whose default_rule is null must come from the text unless it says "required": false (the board size slots: a primary reference that is not request-sized needs no number, and a request-sized one takes its size from them when they are filled, else from the part-size question; generalize delta 001 D4). The required flag is never shown to the controller.

slots.name: board_width
slots.meaning: the length of the circuit board's longer edge

slots.name: board_depth
slots.meaning: the length of the circuit board's shorter edge

slots.name: keepout_above
slots.meaning: the free height that must stay clear above the board's top surface (component keep-out)

slots.name: keepout_below
slots.meaning: the free height that must stay clear below the board's underside (solder side)

slots.name: board_clearance
slots.meaning: the minimum gap between the board and any printed surface

slots.name: headroom
slots.meaning: the minimum free space required above the tallest part on the board

slots.name: opening_oversize_max
slots.meaning: the most a wall opening may be bigger than its cable plug, per side

slots.name: wall_min
slots.meaning: the minimum wall, floor and lid thickness

slots.name: wall_max
slots.meaning: the maximum wall, floor and lid thickness

slots.name: max_x
slots.meaning: the largest allowed outside length of the closed enclosure (its longest side)

slots.name: max_y
slots.meaning: the largest allowed outside width of the closed enclosure

slots.name: max_z
slots.meaning: the largest allowed outside height of the closed enclosure

archetypes.about: Evidence gates for the archetypes the derivation rules can build (generalize delta 001 D5): an archetype is feasible only when its `needs` hold and the request or an L1 names one of its `evidence` words (text_evidence token runs). Generic vocabulary only; no design names. housing and block are left out on purpose: they name bearing housings and pillow blocks (block archetype, GM5).

tray_lid.source: words that ask for a body enclosing its contents; a generic vocabulary, no design names

face_relations.about: How a text relates the walls two exposed cable connectors face (generalize delta 002 C0). A pair of exposed connectors may take a relation only when one sentence of the request or an L1 names both parts (their part.json names) and one of the relation's evidence words (text_evidence token runs); the controller then reads the relation from the request (one voted enum per gated pair, plus not_stated) and a unanimous reading becomes a face_relation check. Generic English relation words only; no design names or numbers.

same.meaning: both connectors open through the same end or side of the enclosure

opposite.meaning: the two connectors open through opposite ends or sides of the enclosure

fastener_roles.about: Words that say a fastener named in the same clause of the request or an L1 holds the primary board (generalize delta 002 C1): the board screw is the largest such named catalogue screw that passes the board's holes, else the thread the board's mount_holes interface declares, else the smallest screw that passes. The primary's own part.json names count as role evidence too. Generic vocabulary only.

board.source: words a requirement uses for the part held on standoffs at its mounting holes

base.source: a tray prints on its floor without support

lid.source: a lid prints on its flat outer face; the lip points up
